transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I... well, I came in because of my apartment. The people there... they're watching me. Watching when I leave, when I come back. I know they're slipping notes about me to the office. People keep saying it's just regular notices on the doors, but... I know what they're doing.
How long have you been feeling that your neighbors are watching you and leaving these notes?
I don't know exactly... a while. Maybe... a year and a month? Something like that. I just know they've been doing it.
Aside from your concerns about the neighbors, have you noticed any changes in your ability to take care of yourself, hold a job, or manage your daily responsibilities over this past year?

I guess... things have been harder. I don't really go out much anymore. I stopped going to church... or helping out where I used to volunteer. It's just... hard to keep track of the days. I've missed some appointments, and... I think I'm behind on some bills. It's just hard to deal with people right now. I don't really trust them.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?
No. I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just the usual noises.
Have you noticed any changes in your speech, such as having trouble making sense to others or feeling like your thoughts are jumbled?

I don't know... maybe a little. Sometimes when I try to explain things, it doesn't come out right. I'll start talking about the rent, and then... I don't know, the marina, or the choir robes. And the wires in the walls. People just look at me like I skipped half the story. It's hard to get it all straight.
Have you noticed that you have become less interested in your personal hygiene or keeping your living space clean lately?
I don't... I don't really know. I guess things are fine. I mean, I shower when I need to. The apartment is... it's just an apartment. I haven't really paid much attention to it.
When you are with your friends or family, do you find that your face doesn't show much emotion, or that you have a hard time feeling excited about things you used to enjoy?
I haven't really noticed. Nobody's said anything about my face. I just... I don't know. I guess I feel normal. I don't really pay much attention to being excited about things.
Have you noticed that your behavior has become so disorganized that you have had trouble performing simple tasks, like cooking a meal or following a basic routine?

I don't know... I guess sometimes things get a little mixed up. Like... at the senior center workshop. I was supposed to be fixing this shelf, but... I just kept lining up all the screws by size. And tapping the table. I couldn't seem to stop doing that. Then the lady there told me to sit down, and... I just stood there. Holding the screwdriver. Like I couldn't figure out how to do something else. I just couldn't switch gears, I guess.
When you were standing there holding the screwdriver, did you feel like your body was stuck in that position, or that you were unable to move even though you wanted to?
No, I... I don't think so. I wasn't stuck. I just... I was just standing there. I could've moved, I guess. I just didn't.
When you find it hard to get your story straight, do you feel like your words get mixed up in a way that makes it impossible for others to understand what you are trying to say?

I guess so. Sometimes. I'll be trying to explain about the rent... and then I'm talking about the marina, or the choir robes... or the wires in the walls. I don't know. People just look at me. Like I skipped a bunch of things. They don't get it.

When you are speaking to others, do you feel that your main problem is that you have strange beliefs about people watching you, or is it more that your thoughts and words feel jumbled and hard for people to follow?

I... it's like I just said. The words. I try to explain about the rent, and then I'm on about the marina or the wires... and they just look at me because I skipped around. I don't really know about people watching me. It's just... the jumbled up part, mostly.
Are there times when you find yourself doing strange or unusual things that you cannot explain, like making odd gestures or acting in ways that seem bizarre to other people?

I don't know about bizarre. I was at the workshop... the senior center. Supposed to fix a shelf. But I just... I kept lining up all the screws by size. Just tapping the table. The lady there told me to sit down, but I couldn't. I just stood there with the screwdriver. Like I couldn't switch to doing what she wanted. I don't know if that's strange.
When you are speaking, do you ever find that your sentences come out as jumbled words that do not make any sense at all, even to yourself?

I don't... I don't know if they don't make sense to *me*. It's just... like I said before. I try to explain something simple, like the rent. And then somehow I'm talking about the marina. Or the choir robes. Or the wires. I just... skip things. And people look at me. I don't know if it's jumbled words, exactly. Just... skipped parts.
